name: National MILO Marathon 2026 – National Finals
short_description: The National MILO Marathon 2026 National Finals, the season-ending race of the MILO Marathon series, is set for Sunday 6 December 2026 in Clark City, Pampanga, Philippines.
ai_summary: The National MILO Marathon 2026 National Finals is the season-ending race of the MILO Marathon series, scheduled for Sunday 6 December 2026 in Clark City, Pampanga, Philippines, according to the official 2026 calendar. Organised by RUNRIO Inc. for MILO, the 2025 finals offered 42.195 km, 21.1 km, 10 km, 5 km and 3 km races, plus categories for runners with disabilities. The marathon is open only to runners who qualified at a regional leg; the shorter races have open entry.
pros: The season-ending national final of the MILO Marathon series
Water every 1.5 to 2 km and 20 ambulances on standby in 2025
Fast front of the field: 2:27:58 won the 2025 marathon
Qualifiers race the marathon free, with prize money for the top three
cons: Marathon places only for runners who qualify at a regional leg
Six-hour limit with enforced checks at 21 km and 32 km
Night starts: 2am for the marathon in 2025
Overseas runners can take part but cannot win

faqs.question: Where is the race held?
faqs.answer: The National MILO Marathon 2026 National Finals takes place in Clark City, Pampanga, Philippines. The organiser, RUNRIO Inc., has not yet published a specific start venue. The 2025 finals in Iloilo City started and finished at La Paz district plaza, with each distance run on a different route.

faqs.question: When is the race date?
faqs.answer: The official 2026 MILO Marathon calendar lists the National Finals for Sunday 6 December 2026 in Clark City, Pampanga, and notes that dates are subject to change. The 2025 finals started before dawn: the marathon at 2am, the half at 3am, the 10 km at 3.30am, the 3 km at 5.30am and the 5 km at 5.35am.

faqs.question: What distances are offered?
faqs.answer: The 2025 finals offered a 42.195 km marathon, a 21.1 km half marathon, 10 km, 5 km and 3 km races, plus 3 km, 5 km and 10 km categories for runners with disabilities. The marathon is for qualifiers only: runners earn a place by meeting age-group qualifying times at a regional leg. The 2026 categories have not been published.
